records.name: Guatemala

adds.title: Every Day I Live in Fear: Violence and Discrimination Against LGBT People in El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras, and Obstacles to Asylum in the United States (Human Rights Watch)
adds.summary: HRW (7 Oct 2020), Guatemala chapter: 'Guatemalan authorities facilitate anti-trans violence is by placing trans women in men's prisons, exposing them to violence, including sexual assault.' Bárbara Herrarte, trans activist with Redmmutrans (Red Multicultural de Mujeres Trans), described her time in a men's prison: 'Always, at night, someone got in my bed and forced me to have sex with him.' Documents birth-sex placement in the men's prison system as of 2020 with sexual-assault risk, and no gender-identity-based placement policy, special trans unit, or trans-specific solitary/segregation practice; LGBTQ org Lambda flags forced internal displacement from violence generally, but no trans-specific custody-policy or court ruling is documented in the report.

records.note: Guatemala placement practice: HRW (Oct 2020) states the authorities place trans women in men's prisons (birth-sex placement), exposing them to violence including sexual assault, and quotes Redmmutrans activist Bárbara Herrarte's account of sexual abuse inside a men's prison. No statute, regulation, or court ruling setting placement by gender identity was found; no dedicated trans custody unit and no trans-specific solitary/segregation practice is documented in the sourced material. The HRW report is dated as-of-2020; no later policy change was located within budget.

records.name: Paraguay
records.note: no prison-housing data found: no fetchable source documenting where trans prisoners are housed in Paraguay could be located within budget. The 'LGBTQ rights in Paraguay' Wikipedia article contains no prison-placement content (its Penal Code/penal-execution references concern substantive criminal law, not trans custody provision); the 'Travesti (gender identity)' article mentions Paraguay only for the 1980s Palmieri Case (20 travestis arrested under the Stroessner dictatorship) — historical political arrests, not placement practice. No special trans unit, no solitary/segregation practice, no court ruling or policy on trans prison placement is documented; the record retains the prison-housing data gap.
